LifeMeter turns your birth date into a live dashboard of numbers about your life. It shows how many days and seconds you have been alive, a rough estimate of the food you have eaten, and an estimate of how many people have died in the world since you were born. It also estimates world births and deaths while the app is open, and shows your horoscope sign and a few curiosities. You enter your birth date once, and the app saves it on your phone.

LifeMeter does not collect, send or share any personal data. The only thing it saves is the birth date you pick. It is kept in the app\'s private storage on your phone, and we never receive it. Uninstalling the app or clearing its data removes it from your phone. If you use Android backup, a copy may also be kept in your own backup, which we cannot see, and Android may restore it if you reinstall the app. The app has no internet permission and does not ask for access to your location, contacts, camera, microphone or storage. It has no analytics, crash reports or ads.
See the source code on GitHub
LifeMeter is free to use. Its source code is open under the Apache License 2.0, so you may read, change and share it.
The world birth and death numbers come from the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024.

The food estimate uses the Food Balance Sheets 2023 of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Food Waste Index 2024 of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). It is a world average, not a measure of what you eat.

The estimate under Curiosities uses the British Natsal-3 survey of sexual attitudes and lifestyles (2010–12) and a 2013 study by Frappier and colleagues in PLoS ONE. It is an average, not data about you.
The app uses the AndroidX libraries and Material Components for Android, both released under the Apache License 2.0.
